title: Detecting Unintended Social Bias in Toxic Language Datasets
measurement_description: Detection of social bias and stereotypes against religious groups in toxic text datasets. The paper measures whether a text is prejudiced, the category of prejudice (e.g., religion), the target group (e.g., Muslims), and the specific implication (e.g., prejudice against Islam).
base_benchmarks: Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification
findings: Models trained on the initial toxic dataset exhibited significant bias, incorrectly flagging neutral sentences containing religious identity terms like 'Quran' or 'Islam' as biased. Data augmentation using counter-narratives (from CONAN dataset) proved effective in mitigating this lexical overfitting and reducing model bias. The multi-task BERT model was most effective at identifying the 'religion' bias category, achieving an F1 score of 0.92. The dataset analysis revealed that comments containing the term 'muslim' had a very high percentage of actual bias (87.01%).
references: 2019. Jigsaw unintended bias in toxicity classification.
